confirmed.title: A real failure inside decide() is reported as 'Things changed', so send-back can loop forever and the real error is never shown
confirmed.detail: In `_Red.confirm` the `except (UserError, AccessError)` block decides whether the plan was 'stale' by re-reading `request.lock_revision`, `current_step_key` and `inbox._is_mine(request)`. It does this while still INSIDE the runner's savepoint, before that savepoint is rolled back (`invalidate_recordset()` flushes first). `engine.decide` creates the decision, calls `request._bump_lock()`, writes `state='returned', current_step_key=False`, and only then calls `record._approval_return(...)`, which the engine does not wrap in a try (unlike `_approval_reject` and `_tell_record_it_moved`). If that adapter call raises, the half-written row is what PayAI reads: the lock moved, the step key is False and it is not 'mine', so it raises `Stale`. The runner rolls back, sets the task to planned, then `_fresh_card` builds an identical plan with the same lock revision and the note 'Things changed since I showed you this plan… nothing was done'. Typing SEND BACK again fails the same way. The real reason (an AccessError the Approvals inbox would show) never appears, and the task's `error` records 'changed since the plan was shown'. The same misreading happens for any exception after `_bump_lock`, for example in `_activate_next` or in the facade's `get_request` after the engine call. Test 09 only covers a bump made BEFORE `decide` runs.
confirmed.repro: Route: step 1 'HR Manager check' held by user F. F reads pay runs through `pb_hr_payroll_base.group_payroll_analytics_user` (read-only on hr.payslip.run, so the engine's `record.check_access('read')` passes) but has no write right on hr.payslip or hr.payslip.run.
